title: Kuk Early Agricultural Site
note: Independent invention of farming in highland New Guinea: mounds for banana, taro and yam c. 7,000–6,400 years ago, ditch drainage from 4,000 BP, possibly from 10,000 BP. UNESCO WHC 887 (S5 47 1.36 E144 19 54.2, 116 ha, 1,500 m). Needs Denham et al. 2003 (Science) for dates; place record importance >= 3 needs a model. Under-recorded Pacific.

title: Pearl millet domestication in the West African Sahel
note: Fully domesticated pearl millet in the Lower Tilemsi Valley, Mali, as early as 2500 BC, unambiguous by 2000 BC; eastern Mauritania by 1700 BC; dispersal to India by end of 3rd millennium BC (Winchell et al. 2018, Afr Archaeol Rev, open access at UCL Discovery; Manning et al. 2011). Pair with sorghum in the eastern Sahel (Butana Group).

title: Early farming in the Ñanchoc Valley, northern Peru
note: Squash (9240 ± 50 14C BP seeds), peanut, Phaseolus beans and pacay; farming system in place by ca. 8,600 cal BP (Piperno & Dillehay 2008 PNAS, PMC2604935; Dillehay et al. 2007 Science). Andes before 1492 is under-recorded.

title: Plant domestication in eastern North America
note: Indigenous domestication of squash (Phillips Spring, MO, 5,025 cal BP), sunflower (Hayes, TN), marshelder (Napoleon Hollow, IL) and chenopod (Cloudsplitter, KY, 3,700 cal BP) (Smith 2006 PNAS, PMC1567861; Smith & Yarnell 2009 on the crop complex at 3800 BP). Indigenous peoples of the Americas before 1492.

title: Rice domestication in the Lower Yangtze (Shangshan)
note: Phytolith-dated rice at Shangshan (29°27′21.6″N 119°58′15.4″E) from 9,400 cal BP, Hehuashan, Huxi (Zuo et al. 2017 PNAS, PMC5488950). Shangshan culture c. 11,000–8,600 cal BP.

title: Çatalhöyük
note: Neolithic settlement in central Anatolia, c. 7100–5950 cal BCE, peak population 3,500–8,000; health, workload and violence data (Larsen et al. 2019 PNAS, PMC6601267). UNESCO listing number to verify. Needs a model (place, importance >= 3).

title: Maize domestication in the Central Balsas Valley
note: Maize and squash at Xihuatoxtla shelter (964 m, near Iguala, Guerrero) by 8,700 cal BP; progenitor Balsas teosinte (Piperno et al. 2009 PMC2664021; Ranere et al. 2009 PMC2664064). Site coordinates still needed.
